name: Write a LinkedIn post
when: The founder wants a LinkedIn post about something that happened, a lesson, a number or a launch.
procedure: Ask for the material and wait: the moment, fact or number the post is about, and who should read it. Never invent any of them.
Pick one post shape: story, list, contrarian, lesson or question. Pick two different hooks, e.g. an odd-precision number and a dated reversal.
Write line one as a statement or a number under 140 characters. Never a question, never "Here's what", never "Stop X, start Y".
Write the body: 900 to 1,300 characters, one or two sentences a paragraph, a blank line between ideas, at most one contrast and one list of three.
Close with a specific question about the reader's own experience, not "Thoughts?". Put any link in the first comment, never in the body.
Run the "Humanize a draft" skill on both versions, then give version A and B with each hook named. The founder posts it by hand.
pitfalls: Two hooks blended in one post weaken both: one hook per version.
A round number ("almost $5k") reads as made up; use the exact one the founder gave, with what it refers to.
More than three hashtags, or any in the middle of a sentence, looks like spam.
verify: Two versions exist; each first line is under 140 characters and is not a question; each is 900 to 1,300 characters; no link in the body; every number and name came from the founder.
